title: Reproducing Reed 1989: how fast hydrogen anneals interface traps

sample.paper: a review: “In this paper the contributions of several of these models are surveyed.”
sample.ours: three cases built from its figures
sample.note: The samples are the cited papers'; the review gives only what its figure captions say about them.

sample.paper: aluminium gate (Figures 2 and 3); bare oxide for Brower (Figure 1)
sample.ours: GATE: Al (recorded; no program reads it)
sample.note: The gate is the hydrogen source in Reed's account; no statement can say so.

sample.paper: not stated for any data set
sample.ours: an assumed dry oxidation, 1000 °C for 1 h, searched

sample.paper: Figure 2: 8.4×10^10 cm⁻² eV⁻¹ at t = 0, after three metallisations; Figure 3: no t = 0 point
sample.note: The language cannot state a measured starting density; only a history that produces one.

history.item: Dry oxidation that made the traps (Burte and Matthies; not stated in the review, assumed 1000 °C, 1 h)
history.paper: not stated: the review gives no oxidation for any of the three data sets
history.ours: RUN Oxidation DURATION 3600 TEMP 1000->1000 AMBIENT dry_O2
history.note: The trap-density program needs a dry-oxygen step to start from; the value before the anneal depends on it, so its time and temperature are unknowns.

history.item: Three separate aluminium metallisations, each able to anneal traps partly
history.paper: “which involved three separate metallisations, each of which could partially anneal the Si-SiO2 interface traps.”
history.note: Their temperatures and times are not given; Reed attributes the low starting density to them.

history.item: Midgap Dit by C-V before any forming gas
history.paper: “Midgap Dit against anneal time”; “characterised by CV measurements”
“T = 240 C, p(H2) = 760 Torr”, relative Pb0 intensity from 5.9 to 2.0 over 389 min (Figure 1)
history.ours: not simulated: a relative intensity cannot be compared with a density
history.note: Compared by its rate in the alignment text.

history.paper: “10-25 % hydrogen ... between 400 and 450 C for 10-45 min”
